title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues

- Identifies and escalates quality of care issues through established channels.

- Utilizes negotiation skills to secure appropriate options and services necessary to meet the member’s benefits and/or healthcare needs.

- Utilizes influencing/ motivational interviewing skills to ensure maximum member engagement and promote lifestyle/behavior changes to achieve optimum level of health.

- Provides coaching, information and support to empower the member to make ongoing independent medical and/or healthy lifestyle choices.

- Helps member actively and knowledgably participate with their provider in

healthcare decision-making.

Monitoring, Evaluation and Documentation of Care:

- Utilizes case management and quality management processes in compliance with regulatory and accreditation guidelines and company policies and procedures.

  • Candidate must reside in the Southwest Side of Chicago, IL (Applicable Zip Codes: 60402, 60513, 60534, 60632, 60609, 60629, 60638, 60458)

  • 2 years experience in behavioral health, social services or appropriate related field equivalent to program focus

  • Case management and discharge planning experience

You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.

Job highlights

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.

In this role, you will:

  • Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

  • Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

  • Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

  • Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

  • Conduct virtual visits as needed

  • Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:

As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD

The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Job Description

Job Purpose and Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate CVS Health’s HeartAtWork behaviors, Helping With Heart Actions, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose of “Bringing our Heart to Every Moment of Your Health” by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health

  • Following WeCARE workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment

  • Contributing to positive patient experiences by Helping With Heart: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems

  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist

  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation

  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices

  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.

  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients

  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business

  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security

  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines

  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions

  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements

  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Primary Job Duties & Responsibilities:

1. Prescription Fulfillment and Inventory Management -45%

  • Takes direction from the Pharmacist-on-duty and models best-in-class workflow excellence throughout the shift; rotates through workstations as directed by the workstation assignment board and/or Pharmacist or Lead Technician

  • Production: Produces prescriptions in accordance with WeCARE workflow SOPs, including but not limited to accurate product selection, counting, labeling, photographing, and bagging prescriptions (where applicable) under direct Pharmacist/Pharmacist Manager supervision; follows inventory management best practices (such as utilizing the return-to-stock vial first and dispensing in manufacturer packaging when able) while in production to improve pharmacy inventory excellence

  • Drop-off: Triages prescriptions for data entry, inventory availability, insurance claim processing, and insurance rejection resolution

  • Completes inventory tasks as directed by pharmacy systems and Pharmacist-on-duty or Lead Technician/Inventory Specialist:

  • Timely check-in and shelving of delivered product in appropriate bays

  • Product cycle counts

  • Waiting bin inventories and returns-to-stock

  • Pulls outdates and complete one-by-one returns

  • Takes telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calls prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation

  • Uses good judgment to engage Pharmacist for clinical oversight and support when needed; proactively calls for backup and/or asks for help as required by real-time business needs

  • Collaborates with and supports other pharmacy team members to keep workflow on-track

  • Helps to maintain a clean and neat pharmacy environment (e.g., vacuuming, dusting shelves, trash removal, etc.)

2. Customer Service and Patient Care -45%

  • Brings a patient-centric mindset to all workstations, especially pick-up and drive-thru, Helping with Heart and showing empathy in interactions with customers and other colleagues

  • Demonstrates our purpose during all patient interactions at pick-up and drive-thru, operates pharmacy register and delivers patient service offerings as directed by system prompts and/or guidance of the Pharmacist-on-duty; monitors the length of the line and proactively calls for backup from Technicians and/or the front store team (as allowed by state Board of Pharmacy guidelines) to manage customer wait times

  • Engages patients at pick-up with applicable service offerings, including and especially closing immunization gaps, maintaining integrity and customer-orientation in the delivery of all register prompts, and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for required counseling as directed by the system

  • Welcomes and encourages walk-in immunization opportunities; promptly flags these opportunities to keep patients healthy; proactively schedules patients to return for an appointment to close immunization gaps, when needed

  • Shadows Pharmacist and offers to counsel/fields medical questions, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist; directs the patient to the Pharmacist-on-Duty, as needed

  • Solicits information on a patient’s medical history to provide appropriate medical advice, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist; communicates and interacts with all healthcare professionals to provide optimal care

  • Is knowledgeable and engaging when talking to patients about our digital and loyalty offerings; welcomes and encourages patients to add front store products to their pharmacy order at pick-up

  • Answers the phone and/or returns patient voicemails promptly, using the Helping with Heart actions to understand and address patient requests

  • Executes telephonic patient outreach as directed by Patient Care Central and/or the Pharmacist-on-duty; brings a spirit of Helping with Heart to engage patients to improve health outcomes

  • Steps in to support pharmacy team with challenging patient interactions, when needed; uses good judgment to escalate challenging patient interactions to the Pharmacist-on-Duty, when needed

  • Delivers additional health care services as allowable by state regulation, individual certification, and as directed by pharmacy leadership team, including but not limited to point-of-care and/or swab-and-send testing, immunization preparation and/or delivery, etc.

  • Delivers service excellence by walking patients to the product in the aisle, when applicable

3. Continuing Training, Compliance, and Pharmacy Team Culture - 10%

  • Completes required ongoing compliance and role-based training in a timely manner, including maintaining certification and/or licensure as required by state Board of Pharmacy

  • Practices and develops skills performed by pharmacists, when applicable and according to state law

  • Partners with assigned preceptor to ensure participation in, and completion of, Key Learning Experiences (KLEs) specified for this intern year

  • Completes required monthly quizzes and other regular knowledge checks

  • Attends all required service huddles and/or action planning meetings

  • Regularly reviews communications (e.g., email, myWork, etc.) via computer, ironman, binders, and/or bulletin board to maintain awareness of pharmacy priorities, action plans, and changes to store processes and procedures

  • Listens and responds to feedback from the Pharmacist-on-duty; provides thoughtful and constructive feedback to peers and leaders; plays an active role in building a positive team culture where all colleagues feel safe, included, valued, and empowered

  • Complies with CVS Workplace Policies, including meal and rest break policies, bag check policies, and CVS Timekeeping and Payroll Practices policies regarding proper clocking in and out, and not working while off the clock

Education:

High School Diploma or General Equivalent Development (GED) - required

Other Certification(s): Eligibility to immunize - preferred

Other License(s): active Pharmacy Intern License in state where district is located - required

Prior Relevant Work Experience:

1 to 3 years - preferred

Essential Qualifications and Functions:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy

  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends

  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe

Attention and Focus:

  • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time

  • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs

  • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety

Customer Service and Team Orientation:

  • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner

title: Physician Associate Student Rotation (Posted 7/23/26)
description:
For Physician Associate Student Rotations in CT, DC, GA, MD, MN, NC, NE, NV, RI, SC, TN, TX

This clinical rotation prepares Physician Associate students for ambulatory care settings. MinuteClinic accomplishes this goal by not only meeting the academic standards of the school, but by providing students with a well-rounded experience that includes specialized online training, patient interaction, visibility to our EMR and the opportunity to work in a new and exciting model of health care. Our preceptors have a passion for teaching and sharing their knowledge. All of our providers have exceptional clinical skills and are experts in the operational skills required to run their own clinic. MinuteClinic’s student rotations offer the most unique experience available, because you are doing more than just enhancing your clinical skills: Practical education including clinic operations, insurance procedures, and reference of evidence based guidelines. Students will gain exposure in an ambulatory care setting and develop an understanding of how these clinics fit into the current structure of health care delivery. Patient care includes patients 18m and older for acute and chronic care including women's health exams, DOT physicals, sports physicals, etc. You’ll develop an understanding of how our corporate office relates to and supports our clinical practice. MinuteClinic is open 7 days a week and our providers’ schedules are compressed, so clinical days can vary from week-to-week. Clinic locations may also vary depending on schedule of your assigned preceptor.

Required Qualifications:

To participate, you must be enrolled in a Physician Associate program that already has an executed Affiliation Agreement with MinuteClinic. PA students are only eligible for clinical rotations in the states in which we currently hire PAs. We will also verify with your program faculty that you are eligible for a clinical rotation at MinuteClinic. If your program deems you as eligible for consideration, you will be considered for placement.

title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Health is everything. At CVS Health, colleagues are committed to increasing access, lowering costs, and improving quality of care. Millions of times a day, we help people on their path to better health –from advising on prescriptions to helping manage chronic and specialty conditions. As a 3rd year pharmacy intern, you have a significant role in our company working as a part of the pharmacy team– delivering our purpose, modeling our values, and demonstrating genuine, authentic care for our patients.

While working as a 3rd year pharmacy intern, under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist, you play a critical role in ensuring a safe and effective Retail Pharmacy work environment that delivers exceptional care to each patient. This includes but is not limited to:

  • Regulatory Requirements
  • Quality Assurance
  • Customer Service
  • Inventory Management
  • Workflow Management excluding final prescription verification

Primary Roles and Responsibility:

  • Lead with Heart – display empathy and compassion for your patients, customers, caregivers, and colleagues on your team
  • Seek new ways to grow, collaborate with others, and deliver better outcomes
  • Align others around our purpose to bring your heart to every moment of your health and gain support and commitment

  • Accepted into or actively enrolled in an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy

  • 0-3 years relevant work experience

  • Strong communication and presentation skills
  • Complete all required training within state guidelines and required timeframe
  • Ability to:
    • Have regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Finger Dexterity: Picking, pinching, typing or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Reach overhead; able to stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Precision control: able to adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree and requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Visual Acuity: Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Able to orally communicate information and instructions to colleagues and customers
    • Occasional lifting of up to 20 lbs; exerting up to 20 lbs. of force occasionally and/or up to 10 lbs. of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects

title: Pharmaceutical Reporting Senior Analyst
description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary:
The Sr. Analyst, Pharma Reporting will be responsible for ensuring the successful delivery of pharmaceutical manufacturers' (Pharma) contractual reporting requirements and providing post-production support for Pharma's data and reports. Key responsibilities include:

  • Reviewing and redlining Pharma's data reporting contracts to ensure that reporting requirements, including data quality and specifications, are clearly understood and adequately captured within the contract.
  • Assessing the feasibility of delivering data according to Pharma's contractual needs by conducting necessary research within our Specialty Pharmacy systems and collaborating with our Specialty data systems partners.
  • Collaborating with CVS Specialty & Retail Trade teams to understand upcoming data project needs and product pipelines while providing relevant updates on project implementations and support activities.
  • Creating and maintaining business requirements documentation based on Pharma's contractual data specifications and ensuring that the requirements are clearly communicated to the project team and other internal stakeholders.
  • Acting as the designated point of contact for Pharma and their third parties (HUBs and Data Aggregators) during contract redlining, project implementation, and ongoing support of Pharma's data and reports. Leading any data-related discussions and addressing data-related questions.
  • Thoroughly reviewing and investigating any data issues, concerns, or questions in a timely manner, and ensuring that any data issues are addressed according to contractual SLAs.
  • Partnering with external and internal teams as needed to address data questions and issues.
  • Conducting root cause analysis of incoming data concerns that do not comply with Pharma contracts to remediate the issue and prevent it from occurring again in the future.
  • Executing and modifying simple and moderately complex SQL queries to combine, parse, extract, and manipulate data to aid in the analysis and resolution of complex data requests/issues.
  • Collaborating with the development team and Account Managers to analyze and collect meaningful metrics and insights for Quarterly Business Review meetings with Pharma.
  • Closely tracking Pharma reporting projects/intake for successful delivery.
  • Handling other responsibilities that may arise related to servicing data requests for our Pharma clients.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:
1. Creating and reviewing business and technical documents and contract language pertaining to data reporting requests by pharmaceutical manufacturers to demonstrate understanding of data commitments and implications for the business (15%). Ensuring production inquiries are resolved in a timely manner, reviewing, problem-solving, and conducting root cause analysis of incoming data concerns that do not comply with Pharma contracts (20%). Analyzing data and reporting information from data feeds and warehouses to determine the feasibility of data reporting requests from pharmaceutical manufacturers (10%). Tracking project implementations or intake for data-related changes (30%). Executing proper maintenance and centralized storage of key project documentation, including business requirements, technical specifications, design documents, test plans, etc. (10%). Writing and executing simple and moderately complex SQL queries to combine, parse, extract, and manipulate data to aid in data reporting (15%).

Education:
Indicate the level of education typically required for the position and area of concentration. Enter "R" for Required or "P" for Preferred.

  • [R] Bachelor's Degree with a concentration in Information Systems, Mathematics, Computer Science, Statistics, Analytics, Accounting, or other scientific-related field of study, or 4 years of equivalent work experience.

Prior Work Experience:
Indicate the amount of prior related work experience typically required to fulfill the responsibilities of the position. Enter "R" for Required or "P" for Preferred.

  • [R] 1+ years of SQL experience or other relevant programming experience.
  • [P] 2+ years of experience working in a client-facing role.
  • [R] 2+ years of experience working in a professional services environment with clients/stakeholders, preferably in reporting requirements, data reconciliation, and root cause analysis.
  • [P] 1+ years of healthcare experience.

Required Skills:
List specific skills or talents that a qualified incumbent should possess, in order of importance.

  • Experience working in a client-facing role.
  • Ability to influence and build effective working relationships with all stakeholders.
  • A "can do" attitude.
  • Effective oral and written communication skills.
  • Intermediate analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Intermediate MS Excel knowledge.
  • Working knowledge of SQL or other similar programming languages.
  • Knowledge of requirements documentation (business requirements, functional requirements, solution requirements, etc.).

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience reviewing and redlining contractual documents.
  • Experience working in the healthcare industry.
  • Knowledge of Teradata, Google Big Query, Snowflake, and Oracle databases.
  • Strong working knowledge of data reconciliation, reporting, and analysis.

40

Full time

title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
    • Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
  • Mathematical Reasoning:
    • Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
  • Problem Resolution:
    • Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
  • Physical Demands:
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
    • Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
    • ; Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
  • Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
  • Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
  • Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:


$23.00 - $28.00

As health care innovators, we are making quality care affordable, accessible, simple and seamless. title: Executive Director, Distribution Center Operations
description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary:

The Executive Director, RI Distribution Center Operations is responsible for the overall performance of the Woonsocket and North Smithfield Distribution Centers. This leader owns the strategy and execution necessary to deliver exceptional operational, financial, service, safety, quality, compliance, and talent outcomes. The role is accountable for creating and sustaining a best-in-class colleague experience focused on engagement, retention, leadership development, training, succession planning, and inclusion.

The Executive Director develops and executes both short and long-term facility strategies that align with enterprise and Supply Chain objectives while ensuring achievement of profit and expense goals, superior customer service, regulatory compliance, and continuous operational improvement. This position provides direct leadership to exempt-level leaders and maintains oversight of front store and pharmacy distribution operations.

Key Responsibilities:

Operational Leadership & Execution

  • Own full P&L responsibility for the RI Distribution Center, including expense management, profitability, service levels, labor optimization, and operational performance.
  • Deliver timely, secure, and accurate distribution services through effective deployment of transportation and delivery resources.
  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements, including DEA, Board of Pharmacy, OSHA, wage and hour laws, EEO/AA, and other federal and state regulations.
  • Partner with suppliers and vendors to negotiate contracts, optimize supply chain operations, and resolve distribution challenges.
  • Achieve productivity, service, quality, and operational performance metrics through continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Maintain strong partnerships with field operations, transportation, asset protection, and corporate functions to improve service and resolve operational issues.

Colleague Experience & Culture

  • Foster a highly engaged, inclusive, and performance-driven work environment.
  • Maintain strong floor presence and active engagement with colleagues and frontline leaders.
  • Partner with Human Resources to develop and execute colleague engagement strategies using survey results and feedback.
  • Drive succession planning, talent management, retention, and training initiatives across the distribution center.
  • Ensure effective communication across all levels of the organization.
  • Promote accountability for employee experience metrics, including engagement, turnover, retention, and overtime management.

Strategic Planning & Business Leadership

  • Develop and execute short and long-term strategic plans aligned with enterprise and Supply Chain objectives.
  • Translate business priorities into actionable site goals, timelines, and accountabilities.
  • Leverage partnerships across HR, Supply Chain, and corporate functions to develop and refine strategic initiatives.
  • Optimize facility capacity, product flow, and operational efficiency through data analysis and continuous improvement.
  • Drive innovation and support network-wide supply chain strategies and initiatives.
  • Lead through ambiguity and organizational change while maintaining focus on business outcomes.

Talent Development

  • Develop and mentor direct reports to assume increasing levels of leadership responsibility.
  • Build and execute a comprehensive talent strategy focused on leadership development and succession planning.
  • Create robust and diverse leadership pipelines for critical positions.
  • Establish a high-performance culture with clear expectations, accountability, and development plans.
  • Coach leaders on Individual Development Plans (IDPs) and talent growth strategies.
  • Leverage enterprise talent tools and development programs to strengthen organizational capability.

Continuous Improvement & Change Management

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve efficiency, safety, service, quality, and colleague experience.
  • Serve as a change leader by embracing and championing organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Utilize metrics and performance data to drive sustainable improvements.
  • Coach leaders to effectively manage and implement change within their teams.
  • Collaborate with HR and business partners to develop change management strategies that minimize disruption and maximize adoption.
  • Promote change agility and a continuous improvement mindset across the distribution center and broader network.

Required Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of leadership experience in distribution, warehouse, retail, manufacturing, or related operational environments.
  • 8+ years of experience leading exempt-level leaders.
  • 5+ years of experience implementing Lean principles.
  • 3+ years of experience utilizing 5S methodologies.
  • 3+ years of experience in Supply Chain, Logistics, and Inventory Management.
  • Experience leading operations with 300+ non-exempt employees.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive both organizational culture and business results.
  • Proven success developing and advancing talent across multiple organizational levels.
  • Strategic thinker with the ability to align operational execution with business goals.
  • Experience managing regulatory and compliance requirements at federal and state levels.
  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational, time management, and prioritization abilities.
  • Proven ability to independently lead large-scale strategic initiatives to successful completion.
  • Demonstrated success working within complex, cross-functional, matrixed organizations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint) and distribution center reporting systems.
  • Ability to work in a distribution center environment, including frequent standing, walking, and stair climbing.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree (MBA, Master's, or related discipline).
  • Experience with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).
  • Experience leading safety programs and managing OSHA-related compliance initiatives.
  • Strong financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting experience.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent continuous improvement credential.

Education:

Required:

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.

Preferred:

  • Master's Degree.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent continuous improvement certification.

At Oak Street Health, we’re rebuilding healthcare as it should be. The Patient Insurance Navigator (internally known as the Patient Relations Analyst, or PRA) is an integral part of this process and the ultimate patient advocate within our clinics. As our resident insurance experts, they help guide patients through Medicare, Medicaid, and affordable coverage options by answering any questions, navigating complex plans and billing, connecting with insurance resources, and providing critical support during the Annual Enrollment Period (AEP).

PRAs also assist our Care and Outreach teams with high-touch customer service aspects within the clinic, such as scheduling, insurance verifications and billing.

title: In-Home Physician Part Time - Wasau-Merrill
description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part Time Physician to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.

You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.

Job highlights

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.

In this role, you will:

  • Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

  • Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

  • Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

  • Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

  • Conduct virtual visits as needed

  • Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:

As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD

The primary care physician gets a snapshot of a person in an office setting, but with Signify Health, we see things like the number of steps to enter their home, the state of disrepair those steps may be in, and the person’s ability to function comfortably and with ease in their own home. We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

Part-time employees qualify for:

  • Select benefits (see benefits guide for details)

  • Malpractice insurance coverage (during Signify Health-related activities)

  • Supplies and other perks

Required & Preferred Qualifications (MDs and DOs)

  • Active, unrestricted license(s) in coverage area(s)

  • Multi-state licenses(preferred)

title: Pharmacy Intern
description:

In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
    • Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
  • Mathematical Reasoning:
    • Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
  • Problem Resolution:
    • Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
  • Physical Demands:
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
    • Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
    • ; Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
  • Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
  • Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
  • Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

$0.00 - $0.00

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. Through your hands-on experience, training roadmap, Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), and time spent with leaders in your district, you will deepen your understanding of and participate in pharmacy practice and patient care scenarios, build business acumen to understand how to improve pharmacy performance, and develop leadership skills to learn how to engage the pharmacy team and drive business outcomes. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

A US Non-Accredited Foreign Graduate is responsible for contributing to safe and effective operations of the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences by showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. title: Product Manager, Clinician Performance
description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. CVS Business Unit: Signify Health
Location / Logistics: Remote position in US with some travel required

Position Summary

This is an opportunity to own the performance and productivity ecosystem that drives an organization's top metrics from the ground up, through the clinician-facing mobile app experience that field teams rely on daily and the internal management tools that give operations leaders visibility and control at scale.

What makes this role different

Our engineering team operates at AI-assisted velocity: we ship and iterate faster than traditional timelines. That means the bottleneck has moved. The PM in this role is the strategic throughput — translating stakeholder alignment, sequencing priorities, and building the cross-functional scaffolding that lets engineering keep moving. You'll be expected to use AI tools in your own workflow, and you'll be building products with AI at their core.

What you'll own

MySignify Scorecard (Clinician-Facing): The primary performance interface for clinicians. V3+ phases include personalized targets, AI-driven metric transparency, member reviews, and A/B testing frameworks to prove that scorecard engagement translates to real quality improvement.

OCC Clinician Management Module (Manager-Facing): The operations manager's unified workspace for clinician performance, replacing 5+ fragmented tools with a single intelligent platform. You will expand CMM to new user types, build bulk action and coaching automation workflows, and layer in the AI engine that handles routine interventions at scale and surfaces only the most complex cases for human review.

Roles and responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end roadmap for the Clinician Performance product portfolio — MySignify Scorecard and OCC Clinician Management Module

  • Drive product strategy for AI-powered features: personalized coaching nudges, intelligent alert triage, OM recommendation engines, and automated intervention workflows

  • Develop and maintain a rigorous approach to A/B testing and experimentation, with focus on proving that scorecard engagement translates to quality metric improvement across the W2 clinician network

  • Partner with engineering and design to ship features that move the metrics: scorecard engagement (target >70% MAU), OM time-to-action on P1 tasks (<24 hours), and performance lift (+2% quality improvement)

  • Coordinate across a complex stakeholder map — operations management, analytics, clinical success, legal, HR, engineering, and executive leadership — at both pod level and cross-team forums including the Monthly Operating Review

  • Define and track KPIs that connect product decisions to business outcomes: clinician quality scores, OM efficiency, documentation compliance, and time-to-action on performance alerts

  • Conduct discovery with clinicians and operations managers to surface what's working, what's not, and what the data isn't telling you

  • Leverage AI tools in your own workflow to accelerate spec writing, research synthesis, stakeholder communication, and decision documentation

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in relevant discipline or equivalent combination of training and experience

  • 4–7 years of product management experience, with a track record of owning complex, cross-functional products from discovery through delivery

  • Background in gamified or performance-driven SaaS — you understand how to design goal-setting, progress visibility, and nudge systems that motivate without feeling patronizing to professionals who take their craft seriously. Healthcare experience is welcome but not required; what matters is the ability to earn trust quickly with expert users who rely on your product data to manage their livelihoods.

  • Comfort operating in an AI-accelerated environment — you've used AI tools in your product work, and you're excited to build products where AI is a core capability, not a feature add-on

  • Hands-on experience designing and analyzing A/B experiments — you can write a hypothesis, define primary and guardrail metrics, size a test appropriately, and interpret results without leaning on a data scientist to tell you what they mean.

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and stakeholder complexity — this role sits at the intersection of clinical operations, technology, and data, and requires strong instincts for when to push, when to align, and when to ship

  • Strong data orientation: you define metrics before you build, you know how to design an experiment, and you can tell the story of value from discovery through outcome

  • Excellent written and verbal communication — you can write a crisp one-pager, a spec that engineers trust, and an executive summary that drives a decision
